title: compile.ts + sprite.ts: DepthState interface missing letterSpacingKey and restrictKey fields
description:
File: packages/swf/src/compile.ts lines 1001-1016 and packages/swf/src/sprite.ts lines 381-392.

Bug: The DepthState interface (defined inside compileDocument() in compile.ts and encodeDefineSprite() in sprite.ts) is missing the fields letterSpacingKey and restrictKey that are written to the object literal in depthState.set() calls and read in the posChanged check.

compile.ts:1001 DepthState has no letterSpacingKey or restrictKey.
compile.ts:1787-1788 posChanged reads prev.letterSpacingKey and prev.restrictKey.
compile.ts:2118,2314,2333,2706 depthState.set() writes letterSpacingKey and restrictKey.
Same pattern in sprite.ts:381-392, 554-555, 559, 961.

TypeScript strict-mode confirms this with 10 type errors (TS2339 and TS2353).

Runtime effect: when TypeScript is compiled with --skipLibCheck or lenient settings the properties silently become undefined on the retrieved DepthState. The check prev.letterSpacingKey !== thisLetterSpacingKey is then undefined !== '' which is always true for text fields with no letter spacing, causing every text field on every frame to be re-emitted as a PlaceObject2+Move even when nothing changed. For text fields WITH a non-zero letterSpacing, the comparison is undefined !== '5' which is also always true even on the first frame, meaning the first placement already triggers a spurious Move re-emission on that same frame. In symbol timelines (sprite.ts) the same issue exists for all text DisplayObjects.

Fix: Add letterSpacingKey: string and restrictKey: string to the DepthState interface in both compile.ts and sprite.ts.

Acceptance: pnpx tsc -p packages/swf/tsconfig.json --noEmit reports zero TS2339/TS2353 errors for DepthState; a round-trip compile of a doc with a named text field (letterSpacing=0) does not emit a redundant PlaceObject2 Move tag every frame.
